issues.description: generate-stories requires an existing story manifest before it can generate stories, so a fresh checkout cannot bootstrap the dataset.
Configured story dataset directory exists but contains no story files or manifest, so the documented demo path fails without external data.
Default config is loaded from the repository root, which breaks normal wheel installs because config.yaml is not package data.
Package discovery includes only emovec modules and excludes required runtime config/data files.
from_pretrained uses dtype while the declared transformers lower bound may require torch_dtype, making dependency resolution/runtime behavior fragile.
all_token_activations stacks every hidden state for a full batch before filtering tokens, causing very high memory use with the default Gemma settings.
span_mean_activations silently returns zero activations when a character span maps to no tokens, corrupting downstream correlations.
effective_start can return seq_len for one-token sequences, leading mean_activations to divide by zero.
mean_activations does not guard against L == s before assigning 1 / (L - s).
emotion_vectors does not validate that every emotion has samples, so missing labels produce NaN vectors.
pca_components divides by total variance without handling zero-variance inputs, producing NaN components.
load_vectors trusts stale artifacts without validating manifest compatibility, array shapes, model name, or emotion order.
Story generation performs HTTP requests without a timeout and can hang indefinitely.
Story generation sends bearer credentials to arbitrary configured API bases without enforcing HTTPS.
Runtime dependencies are lower-bound only and there is no lockfile, making experiment results and installs non-reproducible.
Project dependencies are also lower-bound only, leaving major-version/API drift unbounded.
The only story-loader coverage is skipped when data is absent, so CI will not catch the fresh-checkout dataset failure.
Generated egg-info and outputs are ignored but are present in the workspace, indicating the tree is not clean for active development.
